nodes.label: NIR Device Link Control (task page drives Arduino stimulation directly)
nodes.rationale: The experiment task page owns the serial link to the Arduino so that stimulation start/stop is bound to the same page that schedules trials, avoiding a second operator page and keeping stimulation and behavioural timing on one clock.
nodes.norm_label: nir device link control (task page drives arduino stimulation directly)

nodes.label: Stimulation Stop-Reason Alert Banner
nodes.rationale: If the NIR/heater stops mid-session (e.g. thermal cutoff) the researcher must see it immediately without watching the hardware dashboard, since a silently aborted stimulation would invalidate the run.

nodes.label: Blinding Indicator Shield (minimalist low-luminosity dot)
nodes.rationale: The study blinding relies on 850 nm NIR being invisible; the participant-facing view must carry no condition-revealing visual cue, so the focus indicator is deliberately low-luminosity and condition-independent.

nodes.label: Session Protocol Summary (17 min = 10 EMG + 7 reaction-time, 5 s + [0,2 s] jitter, SPACE key)
nodes.norm_label: session protocol summary (17 min = 10 emg + 7 reaction-time, 5 s + [0,2 s] jitter, space key)

nodes.label: Device Action Commands (M cycle, G start, X abort, R reset latch, S simulate over-temp)
nodes.norm_label: device action commands (m cycle, g start, x abort, r reset latch, s simulate over-temp)

nodes.label: DS18B20 Contact Temperature Gauge & 60 s Sparkline
nodes.norm_label: ds18b20 contact temperature gauge & 60 s sparkline

nodes.label: Closed-Loop PID Heater Control (NIR-matched target 37.5 °C)
nodes.rationale: The heating-only control condition must reproduce the skin warmth produced by the NIR array so that warmth sensation is not a cue; a PID loop to a calibrated NIR-matched setpoint (default 37.5 °C) is used instead of fixed duty, and HEATER_PID telemetry lines expose duty/temp/target.

nodes.label: Safety Latch & State Monitoring (40.0 °C cutoff)
nodes.rationale: Skin-contact temperature may never exceed 40 °C; the cutoff is a latching state that must be explicitly reset by the operator (R) rather than auto-clearing, so an over-temperature event cannot be silently ignored.

nodes.label: Mode LED Blinding Constraint (mode LEDs off during active stimulation)
nodes.rationale: Indicator LEDs would reveal the active condition to the participant and break blinding, so they are extinguished while stimulation runs and only used for pre-run operator feedback.
nodes.norm_label: mode led blinding constraint (mode leds off during active stimulation)

nodes.label: Serial Data Feed Console with Telemetry/Controls Filters
nodes.norm_label: serial data feed console with telemetry/controls filters

nodes.label: Hardware Pin Reference Table (D2 temp, D6/D7/D8 mode LEDs, D9 NIR, D10 heater, D12 STBY, D13 error)
nodes.norm_label: hardware pin reference table (d2 temp, d6/d7/d8 mode leds, d9 nir, d10 heater, d12 stby, d13 error)

nodes.label: TB6612 Driver Output Panel (PWMA NIR, PWMB heater, STBY enable)
nodes.rationale: On the built board TB6612 STBY is hard-tied to 5 V so the driver is always enabled and the Y toggle is a no-op (board replies "NA"); Arduino-controlled STBY exists only in the optional TB_STBY_CONTROL=1 variant on Pin 12.
nodes.norm_label: tb6612 driver output panel (pwma nir, pwmb heater, stby enable)

nodes.label: One-Wire Sensor Diagnostics (DS18B20 on Pin 2, 4.7 kΩ pull-up)
nodes.rationale: 1-Wire needs a 4.7 kΩ pull-up between VCC and DATA for the bus to latch; without it the DS18B20 is simply not detected, which is the first thing to check when temperature reads as invalid.
nodes.norm_label: one-wire sensor diagnostics (ds18b20 on pin 2, 4.7 kω pull-up)

nodes.label: 10 Hz Live Stream Mode (continuous button/temperature polling)
nodes.norm_label: 10 hz live stream mode (continuous button/temperature polling)

nodes.label: Low-Side Logic-Level MOSFET Switch Topology (24 V NIR rail, separate 12 V heater rail)
nodes.rationale: Each load's + goes to its own supply + and its − to the MOSFET drain so a 5 V Arduino pin can gate a 24 V strip; the heater gets its own rail because its rated voltage differs from the NIR strip's 24 V and must be confirmed before power-up.
nodes.norm_label: low-side logic-level mosfet switch topology (24 v nir rail, separate 12 v heater rail)

nodes.label: Common Ground Bus (all supply, driver and Arduino grounds are one node)
nodes.rationale: Low-side switching only works if the Arduino gate reference and the load supply share a return path; a missing common ground is the classic failure mode where the MOSFET never fully turns on.
nodes.norm_label: common ground bus (all supply, driver and arduino grounds are one node)

nodes.label: frontend-design Skill (Experiment UI design & precision guidelines)
nodes.norm_label: frontend-design skill (experiment ui design & precision guidelines)

nodes.label: Timing Precision Guideline (capture-phase keydown + performance.now)
nodes.rationale: performance.now() is used instead of Date.now() because it is a monotonic high-resolution clock immune to system clock adjustments; capture-phase listening timestamps the press before any bubbling handler runs, event.repeat filters keyboard auto-repeat, and preventDefault stops Space from scrolling the page.

nodes.label: Programmatic Audio Stimulus (600 Hz sine, 10 ms attack / 150 ms decay)
nodes.rationale: Tones are synthesised with the Web Audio API rather than loaded as files to avoid file-load and caching latency that would blur stimulus onset; the attack/decay envelope removes clicks that would otherwise act as an extra transient cue, and AudioContext is created on first user gesture to satisfy browser autoplay policy.
nodes.norm_label: programmatic audio stimulus (600 hz sine, 10 ms attack / 150 ms decay)

nodes.label: Trial Protocol Logic (40 s trial, 5 s + jitter, false-alarm timer reset)
nodes.rationale: A premature press restarts the 5 s + random delay so participants cannot lock onto a rhythm and pre-empt the tone; the randomised offset makes the stimulus onset unpredictable and keeps reaction times reactive rather than anticipatory.
nodes.norm_label: trial protocol logic (40 s trial, 5 s + jitter, false-alarm timer reset)

nodes.label: Blinding-Support UI Rule (plain participant calibration screen)
nodes.rationale: Participants keep their eyes closed during runs, so the participant-facing view is distraction-free and carries no condition information, while all rich status display is confined to the researcher dashboard.
nodes.norm_label: blinding-support ui rule (plain participant calibration screen)

nodes.label: Data Persistence Rule (localStorage mirror + CSV export)
nodes.rationale: Trial results are written to localStorage as they happen so an accidental reload or browser crash cannot destroy an irreplaceable single-session recording; CSV export is the researcher-facing egress.
nodes.norm_label: data persistence rule (localstorage mirror + csv export)

nodes.label: Trial Event Schema (trialIndex, timestamp, eventType, latency)
nodes.norm_label: trial event schema (trialindex, timestamp, eventtype, latency)

nodes.label: Standardised High-Precision Input Capture Pattern
nodes.rationale: Every task in the app must timestamp with performance.now() inside a capture-phase, non-passive keydown listener so that latency numbers are comparable across tasks and never contaminated by handler ordering or auto-repeat.

nodes.label: Storage & Backup Convention (participant-keyed localStorage mirror)
nodes.rationale: Keying the localStorage mirror by participant ID plus timestamp (e.g. nir-pbm-P05-1719246100) keeps runs from overwriting one another and makes traces recoverable after a browser crash or power interruption.

nodes.label: Programmatic Stimulus Requirement (Web Audio / SVG, no media files)
nodes.rationale: New tasks must generate stimuli programmatically rather than play assets, so scheduling accuracy is bounded by the audio/render clock instead of by asset fetch and decode time.
nodes.norm_label: programmatic stimulus requirement (web audio / svg, no media files)
